basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 2:19 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 114. Quid est quod dictum est ingressa esse omnia animalia [ad Noe] in arcam'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 114. Quid est quod dictum est ingressa esse omnia animalia [ad Noe] in arcam (vers. 9)?-- Resp. Non Noe colligente, sed Deo jubente. Sicut dictum est in prima creatione: Adduxit ea ad Adam, ut videret quid vocaret ea (Gen. II, 19). Sic divino nutu coacta animalia, sponte praefinito numero veniebant ad arcam.
